Affiliation:: Qassim University / University Gustave Eiffel / University of Oklahoma
Data & Platforms: IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology (Simulation Environment)
Application Areas: Resilient IoT and Edge Computing Systems
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Digital Twin-Enhanced Federated Unlearning: Integrating Digital Twin simulations with client-level gradient ascent/descent to autonomously detect and mitigate data poisoning attacks in vehicular networks without full model retraining.

Adversarial Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning: Deploying noise generators at edge devices to perturb biometric data (e.g., facial images) before local training, ensuring high-accuracy face recognition while preventing sensitive data leakage to central servers.

Hybrid AI-Driven Resource Optimization: Combining Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) and Game Theory to jointly optimize UAV trajectory, RIS phase shift configuration, and task offloading, thereby maximizing energy efficiency and communication reliability in 6G disaster scenarios.

Unlearning as a Service (UaaS) for Model Integrity: Utilizing Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and gradient-based purification techniques to selectively remove the influence of malicious clients from global models, restoring system reliability with minimal accuracy deviation compared to baseline retraining.
Summary Description: Mohammad Atiquzzaman specializes in securing and optimizing next-generation 6G wireless networks, with a focus on vehicular systems, smart cities, and IoT. His research bridges cybersecurity and machine learning, developing privacy-preserving frameworks like Federated Unlearning and Adversarial ML to protect sensitive data in distributed environments. He employs advanced AI techniques, including Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning and Digital Twin simulations, to solve complex resource allocation problems for UAV/UGV cooperatives and Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS). His work significantly advances the resilience of critical infrastructure against data poisoning attacks while ensuring energy efficiency and low-latency communication in dynamic, disaster-prone urban settings.
